authoring.note:
This is our universes equivalent of NERV HQ. This is an incredibly imposing structure which involves multiple storeys of fortifications. The main building has no windows visible from the outside, though armoured doors and window covers can slide away to let light in some times.

At the north west side of the building there are two large roadways that go inside and another set of security checkpoints. It is a building large enough to drive vehicles into.

This building is said to be like an iceberg where the vast majority of it is underground. This building is constructed on an actual real island and the rest of the artificial island was built around this. The lowest levels of the fortification are actually carved straight from the rock of this part of the island. This building is likely to be incredibly complex in terms of lore, so let's just get the basic concept setup with the note that we'll need to expand this lots later.

lore.summary: Central Fortification is the seat of the Directorate (特別対策本部, Tokubetsu Taisaku Honbu), and the reason this island exists at all: a windowless, multi-storey fortified block on the island's south edge, built on a real rock outcrop that the artificial island was later constructed around. Everyone calls it Central. From outside it presents blank armoured wall -- the covers over its windows and doors slide back only when somebody decides to let light in. Two roadways enter through the north-west face, each with its own checkpoint, both wide enough to drive vehicles straight inside. Most of the building is underground. The lower levels are cut directly into the outcrop's rock, and the people who work there describe it as an iceberg and mean it literally.
lore.playerFacing: A flat grey mass with no windows anywhere on it, sitting where the island's south edge meets the water. Its scale is hard to read at first because there is nothing on the face of it to measure against: no glazing, no balconies, no signage above door height. Two road tunnels open in the north-west face, each with its own checkpoint and its own queue, and vehicles drive in under escort. Every so often a section of wall slides back, there is light behind it for a while, and then it closes again.
lore.gmOnly:
Treat this entry as a first pass that is meant to grow. The brief it was written from says plainly that this building will carry a great deal of lore later and that only the basic concept was wanted now, so add to what is here rather than treating it as a full account.

Two facts are load-bearing and should not be quietly changed. First, the building predates the artificial island: it was built on a real rock outcrop and the island was reclaimed around it afterwards, which means the island's entire geography is downstream of a decision somebody once made about this building. Second, the lowest levels are cut straight into that original rock.

Nothing currently connects that rock to the buried ship or the crater. First Impact happened roughly two hundred years ago on a different island entirely (quarantine/ideas/story/dossier-first-impact.md). Whether anything is in this rock is an open question and a deliberately unfilled blank -- it is the most tempting connection to invent here, and it should stay Ingram's to make.

hooks: The party is summoned to a level they have not been cleared for before, and nobody explains why the meeting is being held that far down.
One of the armoured covers is open when it should not be, and light is coming from a part of the building that appears on no plan the party has seen.
A vehicle goes in through the north-west roadway, and the party has good reason to know it never came out.
activities: Get through the north-west checkpoints, carrying whatever the party is carrying, at whatever Clearance rung they currently hold.
Attend a briefing, a debrief or a disciplinary hearing here, and read the room for who is actually deciding.
Move between levels under escort, and notice how far down the escort is willing to take them.
Petition somebody in this building for a resource, a permission or a person, and find out which of the Directorate's poles is really answering.
scene.history: The outcrop came first. The Directorate built into it, and the artificial island was reclaimed around the result, which is why the island's districts fan outward from this southern edge rather than from its middle. Construction went downward at least as much as upward from the start. How long that took, who authorised it, and what the Directorate's four founders had to do with it are all still unwritten. The Directorate is roughly a hundred and ninety-five years old (quarantine/ideas/story/blank-inheritance-master-timeline.md), so there is a great deal of room here, and it has been left empty on purpose.
scene.consequences: Access to this building is the clearest available expression of the Clearance ladder (design/strategy-layer.md). Every rung the party earns should visibly change how far in they get and how far down, so decide before a scene which levels their current rung actually opens. Write down which levels they have been admitted to, and never quietly walk that back: losing access they used to have is a real consequence and should be played as one, with a reason attached. This building is the campaign's main instrument for making 'you are trusted now' a physical fact rather than a line of dialogue.
